recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Convert to one ratio
steps.margin_note: First mark. The equation mixes cos² with sin, so replace cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ. Everything is then in sine alone and it becomes an ordinary quadratic.

recall.must_convey: That cos²θ is replaced by 1 − sin²θ so the equation becomes a quadratic in sinθ alone.
accept: replace cos squared by one minus sin squared so everything is in sine
convert to a single ratio using the Pythagorean identity
it becomes two sin squared plus root three sin minus three equals zero
cos square ni one minus sin square ga marchi, sine lo quadratic ga marchali
get everything into sine

steps.why: A trig equation with two different ratios cannot be factorised. Reducing to ONE ratio is what turns it into ordinary algebra.
common_mistakes: Replacing sin²θ instead and leaving a cosine behind.
Sign slip when multiplying out the −2.

steps.label: Factorise the quadratic
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Split the middle term: 2√3 sinθ − √3 sinθ gives √3 sinθ, and the pairs then share a bracket.

accept: split the middle term and factorise to two sin theta minus root three into sin theta plus root three
factorise the quadratic in sine
the factors are two sin minus root three and sin plus root three

steps.why: Treating sinθ as a single unknown is what makes the factorisation ordinary. Nothing trigonometric happens in this line at all.
common_mistakes: Reaching for the quadratic formula and producing surds.

steps.label: Reject the impossible root
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and the part most often skipped. sinθ = −√3 is about −1.73, and a sine can never leave [−1, 1] — so that branch is discarded, with the reason written down.

recall.must_convey: That sinθ = −√3 is rejected because |sinθ| ≤ 1, and the reason is stated.
accept: sin theta equals minus root three is impossible because sine cannot exceed one in size
reject the second root, a sine is always between minus one and one
that branch has no solution since root three is bigger than one
sin theta minus root three impossible, sine range minus one to one
discard the impossible value with a reason
heard_as: mod sin theta less than one

steps.why: A quadratic always gives two roots, but a trig equation only accepts values a sine or cosine can actually take. Checking the range is part of solving, not a formality.
common_mistakes: Carrying sinθ = −√3 forward and inventing an angle for it.
Discarding it silently with no reason given.

steps.label: Solve the valid root
steps.margin_note: Last mark. sinθ = √3/2 is sin(π/3), so the principal value is π/3 and the sine general solution applies.
lines: Here the principal value is α = π/3
For sinθ = sinα, θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ α

recall.must_convey: That sinθ = √3/2 gives principal value π/3 and general solution θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/3), n ∈ Z.

the principal value is pi by three and the general solution follows

steps.why: Only one branch survived, so there is only one family of solutions — but it is still an infinite family, which is why n ∈ Z must appear.
common_mistakes: Giving only θ = π/3 and no general solution.
